THOUGHT: This is a teenage girl with a large, expansile maxillary sinus/jaw mass that remodels and thins bone, involves the alveolar ridge and molar roots, and causes displacement of the orbit and nasal septal deviation. CT shows a heterogeneous lesion with solid and cystic components. Histology demonstrates a spindle-cell stromal process in a patternless arrangement with numerous multinucleated giant cells, rare mitoses, and no cytologic atypia. That constellation (young patient, jaw/maxillary location, tooth/root involvement, expansile remodeling, spindle stroma with multinucleated osteoclast‑type giant cells) most strongly fits a central giant cell lesion of the jaw—classically central giant cell granuloma (also called giant cell reparative granuloma). Aneurysmal bone cyst (or a combined ABC/giant‑cell lesion) is an important close alternative given the cystic imaging components. Primary giant cell tumor (osteoclastoma) can have similar histology but is less typical in the jaw and often shows more mitotic activity/aggression. Brown tumor from hyperparathyroidism mimics giant‑cell lesions histologically and should be excluded with calcium/PTH testing. Desmoplastic fibroma or other benign fibro‑osseous tumors of the jaw are less likely but possible.

DIAGNOSIS:
1. Central giant cell granuloma (central giant cell lesion / giant cell reparative granuloma) — most likely
2. Aneurysmal bone cyst (primary or secondary / ABC with giant‑cell reaction)
3. Giant cell tumor of bone (osteoclastoma) involving the maxilla — less likely
4. Brown tumor of hyperparathyroidism (metabolic lesion mimicking giant‑cell lesion) — needs lab exclusion
5. Desmoplastic fibroma (benign fibroblastic bone tumor) or other fibro‑osseous jaw tumor
ground_truth: Left maxillary giant cell reparative granuloma (GCRG)
